commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Six-mana Sauron reacts to every opponent spell cast by amassing Orcs; only Army combat damage to a player tempts the Ring, which conditionally discards an entire hand to draw four. Seven Nazgûl make Ring temptations boardwide Wraith counter waves, now including Arcane Adaptation's Wraith Army. Moonstone, Bone Miser and Glint-Horn make optional resets a resource decision.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Bracket 4 — Optimized multiplayer commander-first combat/engine deck. Its six-mana commander, exposed creature/enchantment package, and dependence on opponent casting and combat damage prevent unsubstantiated cEDH claims.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Keep the seven Nazgûl, iconic Ring legends, Army production, Shadow/Army combat and actual Ring mechanics. Reject automatic Consult/Oracle/Breach combo-shell substitution; the deck is distinct from the eight-mana Sauron reanimator in Deck 49.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: All 99 baseline noncommander physical cards reviewed: seven Nazgûl and Call/saga/Bilbo/claim provide temptation; Sauron/Great Goblins/Mauhúr/Barad-dûr/Black Gate build and push Army; Roaming Throne and Arcane bridge amplify all creature trigger sources; Sheoldred/Wheel/Rhystic/Remora give draw and pressure; Anger/Wonder/Entomb and three reanimate spells support recursion; protected Force/Fierce/Swat/Mana Drain/Deluge/Rift cover disruption. See card-role breakdown in the research note.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: Both exact sources have 34 physical lands, 2 Mountains, 3 Swamps and seven Nazgûl; Cavern replaces Rogue's Passage one for one while naming Avatar for a Sauron cast. Mana Vault, Sol Ring, Relic of Sauron, three Talismans, Signet, Dark Ritual and Jeska's Will fund six-mana commander. Replacing four-to-eight-mana flavor with one/two-mana Ring events helps a taxed start but three five-mana+ discard engines remain setup demands.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Targeted answers must contend with ward's actual opponent legendary sacrifice and Lazotep hexproof, while Force, Fierce, Deflecting, Swan Song, Mana Drain, Saruman's Trickery and Rollick preserve stack interaction. Untargeted sweepers still destroy the Wraith/Army board and this list loses Ozolith and two damage sweeps; Toxic Deluge, Rift, Living Death and one-card reanimation mitigate, not eliminate, that risk.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Arcane Adaptation: Creature-type conversion grants the Army Wraith identity; it receives every Nazgûl pump and makes Sauron plus Goblin eligible for Wraith-named Roaming Throne.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Remove the independent four-mana amass-on-own-noncreature-spells creature; enchantment dependence creates an exposed synergy piece. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Lord of the Nazgûl: Five-mana Wraith spell trigger adds bodies for nine-Wraith army plan while Sauron already provides the commander slot.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Loses expensive backup cast-trigger reanimation and an eight-mana high-impact graveyard target. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Bone Miser: Sauron's complete-hand discard makes Bone Miser produce separate creature tokens, BB from land discards, or cards from noncreature/nonland discards.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Five-mana setup and graveyard exposure; weaker if commander cannot trigger temptations. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Moonstone, Harsh Mistress: Discarded cards can optionally go from graveyard to playable exile until the end of next turn, retaining resources through Sauron's voluntary reset.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Four-mana creature vulnerable to removal; choosing exile prevents Animate Dead/Reanimate access and normal costs still apply. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Glint-Horn Buccaneer: Each physical card discarded to Sauron's wheel produces one damage to every opponent; red creature also threatens hasty attacks.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Loses a paid X spell's burst amass, self-mill and free-cast upside; payoff requires Sauron triggers and creature survival. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Herald of Secret Streams: Every Army with amass counters becomes unblockable while Herald survives, turning commander's Army combat trigger into reliable temptation.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Lost one-mana counter banking against wipes; four-mana creature fails against removal/untargeted board sweep. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Lazotep Plating: Instant-speed player/permanent hexproof shields from targeting and amasses Zombie counters onto the Army for Sauron/Goblin triggers.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Removes a three-mana Army-powered creature sweeper; hexproof does not stop untargeted mass removal. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Birthday Escape: One-blue sorcery gives a paid guaranteed Ring temptation and can trip Sauron hand reset plus seven Nazgûl counter waves.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Cuts inexpensive full table wheel, decreases Sheoldred/Archfiend discard and draw burst; Wheel of Fortune retained. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Cavern of Souls: Avatar choice fixes a color for Sauron and can make that creature spell uncounterable, preventing expensive commander tax tempo loss.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Costs repeatable land-based four-mana unblockability and cannot render Wraith spells uncounterable while naming Avatar. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Compared to Soothing of Sméagol: Two-mana bounce of a legal nontoken creature plus a Ring temptation is a tactical opponent answer and cheap commander trigger enabler.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Removes scalable creature mass removal, increasing reliance on Deluge and Rift; bounce fizzles without a legal target. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slots.weakness: Challenged by Fellwar Stone, which could raise tempo or synergy against some pods.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Relic keeps repeatable loot for Anger/Wonder, exact UBR color and Sauron flavor; Fellwar is faster but opponent-dependent.

weakest_slots.weakness: Challenged by Cover of Darkness, which could raise tempo or synergy against some pods.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Siegemaster is independent Army combat identity; fear is useless against black blockers and depends on Wraith typing.

weakest_slots.weakness: Challenged by Dimir Signet, which could raise tempo or synergy against some pods.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Connections pays life for cards/Treasure and independent recurring bodies; cheap Signet improves a narrow tempo window only.

weakest_slots.weakness: Challenged by Gollum, Patient Plotter, which could raise tempo or synergy against some pods.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Three saga Ring temptations and Wraith bodies occur predictably; Gollum is lower curve but requires future death/sacrifice.

weakest_slots.weakness: Challenged by Sam's Desperate Rescue, which could raise tempo or synergy against some pods.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Victimize returns two creatures for one sacrifice at sorcery speed; Sam returns one plus a Ring trigger at a lower cost.

weakest_slots.weakness: Challenged by Orcish Medicine, which could raise tempo or synergy against some pods.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Keep the efficient surviving sweeper against creature swarms; Medicine cannot answer a broad opposing board.

whole_deck_audit.current_baseline_strength: The October 15 baseline is already a commander-first 100 with Call of the Ring, seven Nazgûl, the full amass engines and strong interaction. This candidate preserves its identity; none of ten swaps implies old approval was defective or that every game becomes favored.
whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: Whole-99 baseline role audit, ten exact additions and cut judgments, eight explicitly rejected/retained alternatives, EDHREC no-filter Top Cards and High Lift, Wraith/Orc/Ring theme pages, historical M6 red-team and current legality checks. Two physically complete alternative 100s challenge the ten-swap choice after crossing the five-swap presentation floor.
whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: OFF-RANKED and unranked search specifically identified Arcane Adaptation combining Army with Wraith pumps and all-type Roaming Throne doubling; Moonstone hand-resource access, Bone Miser per-card discard payment, Glint-Horn each-opponent burn, Herald Army evasion, and paid Lazotep Zombie amass. These mechanic-specific alternatives were evaluated beyond a raw inclusion sort.

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Ten 1-for-1 swaps replace high-cost generic/background cards and two redundant sweepers with a coherent Wraith-typed Orc Army, immediate Ring enablers, protected attacks and the optional discard-to-resource/damage subengine. Loses sweep density, early land-based unblockability, Ozolith wipe resilience and one potent wheel; no full win-rate claim.

final_candidate.deckwide_reconciliation: Candidate and October15 baseline raw hashes audited; exact 100 physical cards, 91 distinct names, 34 physical lands, 7 Nazgûl under official up-to-nine exception, basic Mountain x2 and Swamp x3. Ten source removals and ten named replacements; commander remains first and unchanged.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Compared to Herald of Secret Streams: Every Army with amass counters becomes unblockable while Herald survives, turning commander's Army combat trigger into reliable temptation.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Lost one-mana counter banking against wipes; four-mana creature fails against removal/untargeted board sweep. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Compared to Lazotep Plating: Instant-speed player/permanent hexproof shields from targeting and amasses Zombie counters onto the Army for Sauron/Goblin triggers.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Removes a three-mana Army-powered creature sweeper; hexproof does not stop untargeted mass removal. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Compared to Birthday Escape: One-blue sorcery gives a paid guaranteed Ring temptation and can trip Sauron hand reset plus seven Nazgûl counter waves.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Cuts inexpensive full table wheel, decreases Sheoldred/Archfiend discard and draw burst; Wheel of Fortune retained. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Compared to Cavern of Souls: Avatar choice fixes a color for Sauron and can make that creature spell uncounterable, preventing expensive commander tax tempo loss.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Costs repeatable land-based four-mana unblockability and cannot render Wraith spells uncounterable while naming Avatar. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Compared to Soothing of Sméagol: Two-mana bounce of a legal nontoken creature plus a Ring temptation is a tactical opponent answer and cheap commander trigger enabler.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Removes scalable creature mass removal, increasing reliance on Deluge and Rift; bounce fizzles without a legal target. Relative cost is explicitly weighed in the ten-swap review.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Challenged by Fellwar Stone, which could raise tempo or synergy against some pods.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Relic keeps repeatable loot for Anger/Wonder, exact UBR color and Sauron flavor; Fellwar is faster but opponent-dependent.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Challenged by Cover of Darkness, which could raise tempo or synergy against some pods.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Siegemaster is independent Army combat identity; fear is useless against black blockers and depends on Wraith typing.

weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Connections pays life for cards/Treasure and independent recurring bodies; cheap Signet improves a narrow tempo window only.

low_swap_heightened_audit.off_ranked_opportunities: OFF-RANKED direct mechanic discovery beyond inclusion tables: all-type Wraith Throne, Army unblockability from Herald, Bone Miser and Glint hand-discard economics, Moonstone exile choice, new cheap Ring events, and larger/smaller coherent alternative portfolios.

multi_slot_packages.result_and_rationale: Complete exact 100-card higher-count alternative adds Cover of Darkness and Fellwar Stone, but cuts Siegemaster and Relic; gains fear/acceleration but weakens independent Orc Army identity and discard-enabled Anger/Wonder.

Complete exact 100-card early Ring alternative replaces Moonstone and Bone Miser with Gollum Patient Plotter and Sam's Desperate Rescue; improves early creature recursion/temptation but loses repeated discard economics on Sauron's engine.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Retained Relic versus Fellwar, Siegemaster versus Cover and Call versus Phial were challenged after initial ten; none is included just to satisfy a quota. Trimming Toxic Deluge makes the board vulnerable to opponent creature swarms; trimming saga means losing three reliable temptations.
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: The original hand-discard/draw-four is wasteful without cards converting the discarded resources, its large Army can be chump-blocked, and multiple huge Sorceries/creatures overlap existing options; a smarter Wraith typing/cheap Ring package may improve real commander impact.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: Exact finite Wraith/Army, Throne, mana and reset traces show material new interaction value. Against this benefit weigh lost Azolith counters, Windfall draw synergy and Blasphemous Act/Widespread Brutality clear. The proposed ten are a judgment with disclosed counterplay, not measured win-rate proof.

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: Challenge extended to all 99 noncommander baseline slots by role: 34 mana sources; eight protected Ring/temptation sources; seven Nazgûl; Army + shadow/trample/black gate engines; no-spell draw and Wheel/Sheoldred package; six-mana access; reanimation; seven instant stack/protection answers; and actual sweep coverage. Other named challenges Relic, Siegemaster, Connections, saga, Deluge and Call were compared against viable higher-count configurations.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: Fellwar comes online sooner but depends on opponent colors and loses Relic's repeatable looting for Anger/Wonder; selected candidate keeps a thematic independent discard outlet.
Fear adds evasion without four mana but is beaten by black creatures and depends on typing; Siegemaster is proactive Orc/Army combat value without Arcane's enchantment.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: The twelve-change configuration accelerates colors with a two-mana Fellwar Stone and supplies fear to a Wraith-typed Orc Army through Cover of Darkness; both can overcome different mana or blocker pressures.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Relic keeps Anger/Wonder discard, unconditional exact UBR fixing and thematic repeatable access; Siegemaster provides independently useful Orc attack output. Cover fails into black blockers and when Arcane disappears, so twelve is not obviously a better engine.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: All ten selected swaps strengthen actual Ring, Army, Wraith and discard-reset mechanics while paying explicit opportunity costs. The fully physical twelve-change option improves some speed/evasion draws but gives up independent Army combat and discard-to-graveyard access. The early-Ring alternative pays away Bone Miser and Moonstone. Additional exclusions preserve necessary interaction, unconditional upkeep Ring and colored sources rather than chasing swap count.
